articles.title: Christopher Nolan's Underrated 2020 Spy-Thriller Is Perfect Proof of Why Robert Pattinson Will Be A Great James Bond
articles.summary: Warner Bros. Pictures The whole world is talking about actor Robert Pattinson (The Batman) being cast as the new James Bond, after a lengthy search to replace Daniel Craig. With Dune trilogy filmmaker Denis Villeneuve stepping in to direct the upcoming James Bond 26, and acclaimed crime-drama screenwriter Steven Knight (Peaky Blinders) handling the script, there's a high […]
articles.content:
Even after winning fans over as Bruce Wayne/Batman , Pattinson still faces his fair share of skepticism when it comes to getting cast. Some people like to bring up his past role as Edward Cullen in The Twilight Saga , while others question everything from his charisma to his physicality. But there's no questioning whether or not Robert Pattinson can shine in a spy-action role, because it's something he's already accomplished. In 2020 Pattinson gave a scene-stealing performance as a spy whose espionage schemes crisscross between past and future in Christopher Nolan's criminally-underrated sci-fi-spy-thriller, Tenet .

( WARNING: FULL SPOILERS ) Tenet featured Robert Pattinson in the supporting role of “Neil” an agent of the mysterious Tenet spy organization. By the end of the film we learn that Neil is actually one of the first agents that “The Protagonist” (John David Washington) recruits into Tenet. Due to the film's sci-fi twist of inverting time (or “inverted entropy”) Neil spends his career moving forward and backward through time, helping Tenet succeed in its complicated mission to avert a world-ending terrorist attack. More importantly, Neil is the pivotal figure who is tasked with going back in time training The Protagonist on Tenet's mission, operations, and how to navigate the inverted entropy experience.

The two become so close that Neil acts as The Protagonist's guardian angel, both at the start of th film (during a terrorist attack at a symphony) and at the climax, where Niel pulls his own personal “temporal pincer” manuever , saving The Protagonist from a bomb blast in the present, while a future version of himself moves backward through time to sacrifice his life so that The Protagonist can finally defuse a deadly bomb and retrieve a world-ending Algorithm.

Pattinson doesn't get nearly the credit he deserves for his role as Niel. He showcased all of the physicality and charm of a James Bond type, while also having a much more complex internal story to navigtate. Neil isn't just doing spywork aginst the terrorist Sator (Kenneth Branagh) and his forces: he's also having to both finesse and protect his own boss, mentor, and best friend (The Protagonist) through a formative moment in his life, without ever tipping his friend off that he knows him and that they have a long history of espionage adventures still to come.

If Robert Pattinson can handle a spy-thriller as complicated as Tenet , playing a character like James Bond is well within his capabilities.

articles.content:
Months after a " How the Grinch Stole Christmas " sequel was announced, director Ron Howard is setting the record straight on what it would take for the follow-up film to actually come to fruition.

"I just have to caution everybody that Jim [Carrey] and I aren't gonna go forward unless we think we have a great script, and we don't even have a script right now," Howard told People . "We have really good writers and an idea that I'm excited about that I think is very much in keeping with the spirit of Dr. Seuss, his blend of comedy and fantasy. So I'm very pleased with what we have to work with, but I don't wanna make any promises that it's happening because Jim and I are aligned on one thing — we're not gonna go forward unless we believe it has a chance to be great." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to Headline Coachella 2027

articles.title: Jennifer Lopez Revealed The Origins Of The JLo Nickname (And I Had No Idea)
articles.summary: "I never expected it to stick..."
articles.content:
When it comes to celebrity nicknames , is there any better than “JLo”? Jennifer Lopez ’s moniker has been synonymous with her storied career for years. It’s been used in her music, it's her social media handle and has been used to name her fashion, fragrance and skincare lines. Although I just found out about how it started. Honestly, I’m so surprised this wasn’t common knowledge to me until today.

Heavy D was a Jamaican-American rapper who had hits such as “Now That We Found Love”, “Got Me Waiting” and “We Got Our Own Thang” in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The rapper tragically died at the age of 44 of a pulmonary embolism back in 2011. As JLo recalled, Heavy D wasn’t only the first person to give her the nickname, it also inspired her to name her second album, J.Lo . When talking about the origin of the name, she also added this:

The JLo album came out back in 2001, and the rest is history; she’s been JLo ever since. Along with the album title itself, Lopez noted that she also started being called the nickname in rap songs like Pitbull’s “Culo,” Jay-Z ’s “Lost One”.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday’s Steve Rogers Reveal Means an Avengers: Endgame Retcon
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Numerous questions still surround the reveal that Steve Rogers will be returning to the MCU in Avengers: Doomsday, and now, a brand new description has suggested that this return will also mean a significant change to Avengers: Endgame. At the end of Avengers: Endgame, Steve's fate seemed clear. After returning the Infinity Stones to their […]
articles.content:
Clearly, Steve's story wasn't quite the happily ever after it seemed to be, based on his upcoming appearance in Doomsday , and the bonus scenes in Avengers: Endgame Encore only cemented that, as it was revealed that Loki actually arrived and interrupted Steve's dance with Peggy, signaling that this decision to stay in the past may indeed have caused a multiverse-threatening event—which has now been supported by comments that Steve was to blame for the events of Doomsday . With all of that in mind, fans had begun to suspect that the Steve of Doomsday simply wasn't the same Steve who appeared as an old man at the end of Endgame . However, a new Steve Rogers description has seemingly given an answer, and it may very well mean a major Endgame retcon.

For a while, the idea that this might be an entirely different Steve in Doomsday made sense, as it at least explained how audiences could have seen Steve return as an old man in Endgame if, apparently, his decision to stay in the past broke the multiverse. As compelling as that theory was, though, a new Steve Rogers description for the upcoming movie heavily hints that's not the case. Specifically, the description reads, “After returning the Infinity Stones and finally sharing that long-promised dance with Peggy Carter, Steve Rogers believed he had closed the final chapter of his journey. Yet, destiny rarely lets a true soldier rest. When a terrifying new danger threatens worlds across the multiverse, Steve has no choice but to answer the call once again.”

This description certainly suggests that Doomsday Steve will, in fact, be the very same Steve audiences last saw in Endgame (including Endgame Encore ), so that, by extension, means that Steve's ‘ending' in that story almost certainly has to be retconned. The implication, at the end of Endgame , when Steve returned as an old man, was that he had stayed in the past but then lived a happy and full life. However, the emergence of Doom and the very fact that Loki appeared due to Steve's actions, all but guarantee that this will not really be his fate, raising questions about how Steve even appeared as an old man at all. Presumably, both Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars will confirm a rather different end to Steve's story, which almost certainly means a major Endgame retcon.

articles.title: The Most Controversial Star Wars Character Has an Original Collectible That Fans Won't Want to Miss
articles.summary: The Star Wars prequel trilogy wasn't exactly well received when it first released. While opinions on it have softened over the years, and parts of it are even appreciated today, it was quite different in 1999 and the early 2000s. From Midi-chlorians being the building blocks of the Force, to the overall acting, fans tore […]
articles.content:
The prop head was part of a costume rig that actor Ahmed Best wore in The Phantom Menace , along with being the character's voice. Best wore this prop on top of his head, with the actor's face being digitally removed, while rest of the character's body was made out of prosthetics and other practical effects. The head prop is made out of foam rubber, featuring intricate details and eyes crafted out of resin. Lucasfilm decided upon this particular method as it would give other actors proper reference points and eye-lines when interacting with Jar Jar. While the prop and its details look to have mostly withstood the test of time, the right eye has unfortunately drooped a bit, making it look like Jar Jar had a few too many drinks.

While Jar Jar played an important role in the movie, essentially serving as an emissary between the Naboo royalty and the Gungans, George Lucas also decided to make him the comic relief. His speech and mannerisms were clumsy, and naysayers thought it was one of the worst parts of the prequel trilogy. Apart from Jar Jar, Ahmed Best unfortunately also received a lot of toxic hate from fans and critics alike. However, the hate has thankfully simmered down over the years, with many fans also feeling apologetic for reactions. In a moment of redemption Best recently returned to Star Wars as Jedi Master Kelleran Beq in season 3 of The Mandalorian , saving Grogu from the attack on the Jedi temple in a flashback sequence.

With everything that has happened over the years, this Jar Jar head prop is a reminder of the tumultuous reception that The Phantom Menace and Jar Jar Binks initially received. In fact, things have changed so much that fans now look back at the prequel trilogy in fondness. But while Darth Maul, his cool double sided lightsaber , and Anakin's story are constantly lauded as the high points, fans are still split on how they feel about Jar Jar. I personally think it was a miss, but the sheer hate that was spewed because of it was definitely unwarranted, especially towards the actor. No matter how you feel about it now, there's no denying that this Jar Jar head prop is an important piece of Star Wars history, and makes for a fantastic collectible.

Do you think the character of Jar Jar Binks has been redeemed over the years? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Jared Padalecki On Jumping From The Boys Into A Netflix Rom-Com: 'You Really Want To Take A Shower'
articles.summary: On one end, you have wholesome Christmas rom-coms, and on the other, you have...The Boys.
articles.content:
The last time I saw Jared Padalecki , he was – here come some The Boys spoilers – brutally running through and killing people as Mister Marathon. The next time I saw him, he was playing an actor in a wholesome Netflix rom-com on the 2026 Christmas movie schedule . Talk about range. Seriously, I don’t think you can get something more different from a holiday romance than The Boys . So, when I spoke to Padalecki about his new rom-com, Guarding Stars , I asked what it was like jumping between the two projects.

What’s funny is Jensen Ackles also described this reunion as “weird.” Anyway, getting to Padalecki’s comments, he told me that when it came to The Boys , he wasn’t exactly telling his parents or children to use their Amazon Prime subscription to see it. It was gory and wild, so yeah, that left him saying:

Well, considering this reunion was called “one of the most fun and bloodiest hours in all of 2026 TV ,” I can see why Padalecki wasn’t exactly recommending it to children. However, he had a blast, and when it came time to flip the switch from blood, gore and grossness to wholesome Christmas and romance, it wasn’t a problem. He might have Supernatural to thank for that, as the actor explained:

I would imagine that going from playing a wild superhero in maybe the crudest show on TV to working on a Christmas movie that’s made for families would be very fun. You’d get the best of both worlds in a lot of ways, and while whiplash may have been involved, jumping from one production to the other was great for Padalecki.

I mean, Jared Padalecki did, as he said, literally have to take a shower after The Boys ; he was covered in so much blood after all was said and done. Going to do a Christmas movie afterward helped metaphorically cleanse him too.

articles.title: New Doomsday Footage Has Turned the Best MCU Movie into a #1 Streaming Hit Again
articles.summary: Courtesy of The Walt Disney Company What superhero fatigue? Although it seemed for a while that Marvel Studios were losing their edge and their core cinema audience - thanks in part to the arrival of Disney+ and quick turnarounds from theaters to streaming - Avengers: Doomsday is already set to be the biggest movie of the year, and potentially all time. […]
articles.content:
Avengers: Endgame is seen by many as the perfect comic book movie, bringing together a decade's worth of on-screen representations of Marvel Comics heroes in one of the most elaborate and spectacular final acts ever seen. While the movie helped close out the first 11 years of Marvel Studios' highly ambitious output, it was not the end of the story and was, in fact, just the beginning of a new chapter as the MCU headed into a tangled and sprawling branched universe of alternate worlds and fractured storylines. As the Multiverse Saga now concludes with Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars, Avengers: Endgame Encore tells the same story as it did in 2019, but pulls back the curtain on some minor changes and three new moments that completely change the ending of that story .

While Endgame's main story remains unchanged in this new version, the film begins it's changes by extending the final scene in which Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter are enjoying their life together after Steve decided to stay in the past and live through the decades he had missed. In the new version of this scene, their moment is cut short by a knock at the door, with Loki arriving in the costume he was seen wearing in Season 1 of his own series offering to help the couple. What he wants to help with is yet to be seen, but clearly has implications for Doomsday , with Steve returning to the story as one of the main heroes – albeit not as Captain America. A second scene features Bruce Banner in self confinement after the events of Spider-Man: Brand New Day , working on several projects underground where the Hulk can be contained. However, his safety doesn't come with Doom protection and he is spirited away by the Doctor for an unknown purpose, presumably to be part of his army.

The final scene, which was only shown in certain screenings, returns to the Time Variance Authority, with Mobius back working to keep the multiverse in check. As alarms begin to sound, the clearest lead-in to Doomsday arrives with multiple universes colliding, 3000 in total. With the chilling line, “The multiverse is collapsing,” the die is cast, and the end of the MCU as we know it has been set in motion. Yet this is one last glimpse of Doomsday for those who stick around to the very end of the credits, where the chiming sound of Iron Man forging his first suit becomes the sound of Doctor Doom making his own mask. Same mask, different task, as Robert Downey Jr. said when his casting was revealed. How the story now plays out will be seen one of the biggest cinema events in history this December, as Avengers: Doomsday arrives to rule the box office this festive period .

Has Avengers: Endgame Encore hyped you up for Doomsday ? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Is Actually the Most Book-Accurate James Bond Yet, According To Ian Fleming Himself
articles.summary: IMAGE COURTESY OF WARNER BROS. No, we haven't been using a medium to channel a dead author for his opinion. Rather, a look back at what Ian Fleming approved in his lifetime offers some clues that Robert Pattinson is more or less what the author had in mind as a James Bond type. Benjamin Svetkey over at The Hollywood Reporter […]
articles.content:
There's also the sketch, which was meant for a style guide when a British newspaper obtained the rights to do a Bond comic strip. Fleming gave instructions as weirdly specific as, “I think we should avoid giving Bond an American-shaped head and a duck’s haircut,” and the result was the image below:

Well, it took nearly 70 years, and there were plenty of detours along the way, but Ian Fleming finally got the James Bond of his dreams — at least when it comes to jawline and nose shape. https://t.co/kxhNkzetLX

It's a default presumption that accuracy to source material is the best way to go about making a movie, but that's not necessarily true for James Bond. The books began in 1953, and reflect the attitudes of the power structures of the time — by today's standards, Bond isn't just more misogynist than in any of the movies, but also racist. (He's a smoker too, which bumps the MPAA rating up nowadays.) Unless a modern movie is specifically a period piece, and one in which those attitudes come back to haunt him, to boot, there's no way to make that a four-quadrant blockbuster appealing to all audiences. Many of the action setpieces we associate with James Bond are also more endemic to the movies than the books — the version of the character most people like, whichever actor you prefer, includes key components that are not always book-accurate .

In other words, it's no more necessary that Bond match Fleming's description than anything else, which is why names like Idris Elba have floated about over the years. Besides, in 2035, the first Bond book, Casino Royale , enters the public domain in the UK, though not in the U.S. until 2049. So starting in about a decade, you can probably expect British indie filmmakers to try for book-accurate adaptations, minus the aspects added by the films. All that said, it's pretty cool that Pattinson actually does look like the character as written, though that sketch also has something of Roger Moore's eyebrow raise in there too.

As the article notes, however, the newspaper artist wound up ignoring the guide sketch, and drawing a Bond who looked more like Sean Connery eventually would in the part. Nowadays, Fleming could probably exercise J.K. Rowling levels of authorial control, but as with all things Bond, it was a different time. Pattinson is certainly one of the most versatile actors to play Bond; Sean Connery tended to stick to macho roles, and Roger Moore was often mocked for not having much range. That he has the look is really just a cherry on top.

Do you think Pattinson looks the part? And is that a license to kill it in the role? Post your thoughts in comments, for our eyes only.

articles.title: The Wild Way Yellowjackets’ Cast Is Left In The Dark About Spoilers
articles.summary: The final season is arriving on Showtime.
articles.content:
Yellowjackets is arguably one of the best Paramount+ shows , although it required fans to get a Paramount+ subscription including Showtime. I'm personally a hardcore fan who is hyped about the fourth and final season's premiere this month. Folks are hoping to have Yellowjackets ' biggest mysteries solved before it ends its run, and hopefully joins the ranks of TV shows that actually ended well . We know that the series guards it secrets from the public, but it turns out that even the cast is left in the dark about spoilers.

Well, my mind is blown. While Yellowjackets fans are being kept away from spoilers, I had no idea how tight the security was for even the cast. They only got each new script a week in advance, so Nélisse and her costars weren't able to use the full arc of their character to inform each performance. Instead they had to take things episode by episode and play each moment with honesty without looking ahead.

Celebrities: sometimes they really are just like us. Despite being the actors bringing Yellowjackets to life, they were left with episode cliffhangers in the midst of shooting Season 4. I have to wonder if Sophie Nélisse and her co-stars even know all the twists that are coming with the show's final season on the air.

articles.title: 'Wicker' Star Alexander Skarsgard Will Be Pushed Differently for Golden Globes Than Other Awards (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The Golden Globe winner's portrayal of a hunk made of twigs has left many audience members as smitten as — and even envious of — Olivia Colman's lonely fisherwoman who commissioned him.
articles.content:
Alexander Skarsgard , the Swedish actor who has garnered raves — and lust — for his portrayal of a hunk made of twigs in the eccentric dramedy Wicker , will be promoted in an unconventional way this awards season.

The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report that the 50-year-old will be pushed by Wicker distributor Black Bear as a lead at the Golden Globes — specifically, in the category of best actor in a musical or comedy — but in the supporting category at the other major award shows where contests are not segregated by genre. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Alexander Skarsgard to Narrate Quinn Audio Erotica Original Set in World of 'Wicker' Movies 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Powers $31M in Historic Box Office Launch Against Subdued 'Cat in the Hat'

This path — lead for Globes, supporting for Oscars — has previously been employed by numerous others.

It worked well for some. Among them: Tatum O'Neal was nominated at the Globes and won at the Oscars for 1973's Paper Moon ; Maggie Smith won at both for 1978's California Suite ; Catherine Zeta-Jones was nominated at the Globes and won at the Oscars for 2002's Chicago ; and Alicia Vikander was nominated at the Globes and won at the Oscars for 2015's The Danish Girl .

But it was less successful for others. For example, Cate Blanchett was nominated at the Globes but not at the Oscars for 2001's Bandits ; and Steve Carell was nominated at the Globes but not at the Oscars for 2017's Battle of the Sexes .

A Black Bear rep tells THR , “We made the decision to position Alexander in lead actor for the Globes' musical/comedy category because it gives the opportunity to recognize his unconventional romantic performance within the film's unique blend of dark comedy, fantasy and romance. For other awards, where comedy and drama are not distinguished, supporting actor offers a more appropriate path to recognition reflecting the impact of his performance within the ensemble.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Skarsgard, who won a Golden Globe for Big Little Lies in 2018 and was nominated for another for Succession in 2024, delivered his Wicker performance, opposite Oscar winner Olivia Colman, beneath elaborate WETA Workshop prosthetics and a full creature suit . Playing a character who barely speaks, the actor had to exaggerate his expressions in order for them to be visible, but not so much that they would seem over-the-top. The resulting nuanced, tender characterization, with much communicated through subtle gestures and soulful eyes, has left many audience members as smitten as — and even envious of — the lonely fisherwoman who commissioned the wicker man in the first place.

Wicker , based on the short story The Wicker Husband by Ursula Wills, was adapted for the screen and directed by Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson. Its strongest award prospects are probably in the best makeup and hairstyling and best visual effects Oscar races.

articles.title: New Remain Trailer Reveals a Different Kind of Ghost Story From The Sixth Sense Director - WATCH
articles.summary: Warner Bros. Pictures Filmmaker M. Night Shyamalan is no stranger to a ghost story. After all, he’s the man behind The Sixth Sense, a film whose twist took audiences entirely by surprise helped redefine the idea of the ghost story from something centered in a classic jump scare to something much more internal, psychological, and grief driven. Now, […]
articles.content:
In the trailer, which you can check out for yourself below, Jake Gyllenhaal’s Tate Gordon moves into a rental home in a small coastal town and soon encounters a young woman — Wren, played by Phoebe Dynevor — who very quickly turns out to be something much more than a regular woman. It seems that she’s connected to the house and she cannot leave. According to the official description of the film, Wren pulls Tate out of his shell and into the center of a deadly mystery that hangs over the town. The film opens in theaters on February 5, 2027.

Remain ’s Mysterious Woman Doesn’t Necessarily Seem Like The Threat — And That’s Terrifying While there is still so much about Remain that is a mystery and will likely play out in surprising fashion as is the nature of Shyamalan’s films, what is striking about Remain ’s trailer is that Wren doesn’t necessarily seem like a threat herself, but that also doesn’t mean that there isn’t something truly frightening going on. In just the short trailer, We don’t see Wren doing anything particularly dark or disturbing — yes, there is the moment in the bathroom where she’s upset and does attack Tate, but even he says in the trailer that Wren is upset at night. There is very clearly something larger at play and it suggests that Wren may herself be a victim or at the mercy of something bigger and more sinister. Given that we also see Tate speaking with someone who may or may not have their own connection to the supernatural, there could be something much larger going on and no one is safe. Given that most ghost stories feature the ghost somehow being the issue, the idea of Wren potentially being merely a piece in a larger nightmare is interesting.

What is also interesting is that Remain is itself part of something larger and a bit more unique. The film is part of a collaborative project between Shyamalan and best-selling author Nicholas Sparks . The two creatives worked separately on the movie and a novel (Shyamalan on the film, Sparks on the novel) to ultimately come up with the story. Sparks’ novel was published in 2025, but the twists and details of the novel won’t necessarily be the same ones that make it to the screen. That means we have two almost parallel stories to take in that work with the same general concept and it will be interesting to see where they intersect as well as how the romantic elements of Sparks’ work fits into Shyamalan’s film while the thriller aspects of the filmmaker’s work fits into Sparks’ novel.

Fortunately, we don’t have terribly long to wait. While Remain has been positioned as being a Valentine’s Day movie, the film will open in theaters on February 5, 2027.

What do you think about the Remain trailer? Are you prepared for what appears to be a romantic thriller ghost story? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Thomas “Thom” Velde, a longtime head film buyer for AMC Theatres who also oversaw its Canadian operations, has died. He was 83. His family said he died October 31 of cancer in Rancho Mirage, near Palm Springs.

Velde spent more than a quarter-century at AMC Theatres as head film buyer, negotiating film agreements with domestic and international studios. He also oversaw AMC's Canadian ops and real estate ventures.

He joined AMC in 1978, rising to become SVP Film Buyer of its Central Division before being promoted to SVP and managing director of AMC international film marketing in 1998. Tasked in that post with handling film buying policies in Canada, Asia, Europe and other regions, he forged relationships with film companies, distributors and government agencies around the world. Velde's family said was an avid golfer and a devoted college football fan who will remembered for his strength of character, his generosity and the way he made time for the people in his life.

He is survived by his wife, Deborah; daughters Andrea Ter-Velde (John McLoughlin) and Courtney Ter-Velde (Greg Horton); son, Sam Velde; stepsons Matthew Castillo (Crissy Castillo) and Spencer Castillo (Claire Castillo), two grandchildren and five step-grandchildren.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Fans May Not Like the Dynamic Between These Characters, But It Makes Perfect Sense
articles.summary: Adapting a book is never an easy job. But adapting an entire book series for TV, even if it might seem less challenging because there's more room and time to develop the story, can actually be even harder when the source material has a demanding fanbase. Staying faithful is a major concern for many people […]
articles.content:
However, we also had Peter Jackson's iconic The Lord of the Rings trilogy, which made such an impact on cinema and pop culture that it's hard not to hold on to what those movies showed us. So, when The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power made its way to TV, it was only natural that some things would feel strange to fans. Changes were necessary, but just because certain characters act differently or their story arcs don't line up with what we saw in the films doesn't mean they're automatically wrong. In fact, the series is trying to open the door to a new interpretation of Tolkien's work, and now, in Season 3 , that is very important with the dynamic between Sauron (Charlie Vickers), Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), and Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower).

It's understandable why Galadriel and Sauron's connection bothers so many people. After all, she already has a story with Celeborn in the books, where he's her husband, so throwing the villain into the middle of their relationship can feel like a weird choice. But we should remember that disliking a creative decision is not the same as assuming it has no purpose in the story.

Ever since Season 1, when Sauron was still going by Halbrad , we saw there was some tension between him and Galadriel that could lead to a romance. In fact, writer Gennifer Hutchison once said in an interview with SlashFilm , following the season finale, that the intention wasn't to create that kind of relationship, but rather to build “this sort of meeting of the minds and this deep friendship.” Even so, she knew some people would interpret their dynamic as romantic, although her fellow writers weren't quite as convinced that someone would see it that way. And at this year's San Diego Comic-Con, showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay confirmed the new episodes could explore a love triangle, with Bower joining the cast (via Nerdist ).

So, we can't know for sure where all of this is going , but the fact is that The Rings of Power doesn't need to make the nature of their relationship crystal clear to justify the connection between Sauron and Galadriel. And do you know why? What's important is that the Dark Lord sees something in her that other characters might not: enormous ambition and an unwavering belief in her own ability to defeat evil, even when she doesn't always realize she's crossing a line. He knows he doesn't have to convince her to become an evil person; he just needs to make her believe they could achieve something seemingly noble by working together. That's exactly what he tries to convince her of in the Season 2 finale.

Basically, Sauron wants someone who shares his vision of how the world should work, even if that means taking away everyone else's freedom. Galadriel almost falls into that trap, but not because she's in love with him; it's because, at that point, she still struggles to recognize how far her determination can take her. Her obsession with defeating the enemy is tied to her brother's death and the destruction she's witnessed. She has every reason to fight, but that doesn't mean every decision she makes is necessarily the right one. That's the vulnerability Sauron sees and tries to use to his advantage. In an exclusive interview with The Movie Blog , Vickers and Clark discuss their characters ‘ relationship in a little more detail:

And this is where Celeborn comes in and makes things more interesting . After everything that's happened since the days when the villain was still Halbrand, Galadriel will have to deal with the consequences, and her husband could help remind her there's a life and a set of responsibilities beyond the war against Sauron. He could also give her a chance to figure out whether they can still be the couple they once were and build the future we eventually see in LOTR .

Power, corruption, preservation, and temptation are recurring concepts throughout Tolkien's work. In The Letters of J.R.R. Tolkien , the author explains that the Elves created the Rings because they wanted to preserve Middle-earth's beauty and stop everything they loved from fading away. But he also warns that this desire to preserve things could turn into a desire to control everything around them. So, when we look at the dynamic between these three characters in the new season, we can see Sauron representing power and corruption, Galadriel representing temptation and transformation, and Celeborn representing preservation and personal bonds. Their storylines connect in ways that go beyond a simple love triangle.

But sure, you might still argue that none of this is faithful to Tolkien's work , since there's no mention of Sauron and Galadriel having such a direct connection in the past or of her being deceived by him. And then there's her personality, which doesn't really match the character from Jackson's movies, for example. Well, that is character development, one of the most important parts of making a TV show. Still, this approach isn't exactly as far-fetched as it might seem.

Saying that The Rings of Power doesn't take creative liberties would be a lie. But claiming that it makes everything up out of nowhere also means overlooking some of the things Tolkien actually wrote.

There are certainly choices worth criticizing, especially since Amazon unfortunately didn't have the rights to The Silmarillion , Unfinished Tales , and The History of Middle-earth , all of which contain important material related to the events depicted in the show. But when it comes to Galadriel's arc, it's worth looking at the bigger picture. By the time Frodo meets her in LOTR , she's already a wise and powerful figure who also understands the dangers of wanting too much power. When Frodo offers her the One Ring, Galadriel imagines what she could become if she accepted it, but ultimately turns it down. In other words, she's not immune to temptation.

Plus, Tolkien also described the Lady of Lórien as a woman of great physical strength, athletic ability, pride, and ambition. So portraying her as a warrior in the show isn't, by itself, a betrayal of the original material. The same goes for Sauron, who is described as a more complex character than a villain whose only goal is to destroy everything. It's all part of character development: they evolve step by step into the figures we eventually meet in the films. They're not the same people, with the same mindset and perspective throughout their entire lives, and if some fans kept that in mind, they might find it easier to enjoy the series.

In the end, maybe a big part of the audience is too focused on Sauron and Galadriel (and now Celeborn) as a potential romantic storyline, judging the show because of that, when it would be much more interesting to look at the bigger role their dynamic plays in the overall story. They're growing as individual characters, but their interactions also bring out some of the most important matters in Tolkien's universe . You don't have to agree with the series' approach, but seeing it from this perspective could make The Rings of Power more enjoyable.

Head down to the comments and let us know if you're interested in seeing where the show takes these characters, or if you think The Rings of Power has gotten them wrong. Do you have any suggestions for how Season 3 could move their storylines forward?

articles.title: 5 Great Iron Man Armors That Nobody Talks About
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Iron Man is a hero defined by his determination to be ready for anything and always improving his armor designs. Since his debut, Iron Man has developed dozens of powerful and iconic armors that let him contend with Marvel Comics’ strongest villains and heroes. Some of his most popular suits include the Hulkbuster, the War […]
articles.content:
Although Iron Man is content with having these suits collect dust in his garage, their abilities and designs deserve far more respect.

Tony Stark built his first Iron Man suit in a cave with a bunch of scrap. However, when he was flung back to 1,000,000 BC, he had even less to work with. Stranded in the Ice Age inside a cave with powerless armor, Iron Man had to get creative to survive. The result was the Model 66 armor, which combined vibranium batteries, the remnants of his armor, and the surrounding ice. The suit wielded icicles as both blades and projectiles. Obviously, the Ice Armor melted every second Iron Man used it. Despite this massive setback, the Ice Armor was still tough enough for Iron Man to battle Mephisto. As a final gamble, Iron Man could divert all his suit’s energy to fire a single repulsor blast from his chest. Although this energy shattered Iron Man’s suit, it still managed to hit Mephisto’s Time Stone, returning the Armored Avenger to the present. The Ice Armor might have been lost to time, but it’s one of Iron Man’s coolest suits.

One of the most significant events in the Marvel Cinematic Universe occurred when Iron Man discovered the key to time travel that allowed the Avengers to undo Thanos’s snap. In the main Marvel Universe, Iron Man developed a suit that’s based on Doctor Doom’s Time Platform. Nicknamed the Temporal Armor, this powerful suit could open portals, letting the user travel freely through the timestream. The armor's capabilities led Iron Man to deem it too dangerous ever to use. That didn’t stop the villain Sunset Bain from brainwashing Iron Man and forcing him to wear the Temporal Armor. Bain tried to have Iron Man use the armor to prevent the Avengers from ever forming. Thankfully, Bain’s plans were thwarted, and Iron Man was freed from her control. Still, given the sheer number of time-traveling adventures that the Avengers have gone on over the years, Iron Man’s Temporal Armor would be an invaluable asset that he should use more often.

Arguably Iron Man’s most threatening-looking armor, the Model 44 Cold Iron Armor was designed for only one use: killing Dark Elves. Malekith the Accursed and his army of Dark Elves are among the most powerful villains across the Nine Realms. Iron Man accordingly recognized the need for a contingency suit in case he ever had to fight them.. Since Dark Elves are deathly allergic to iron, the Armored Avenger made his first suit almost entirely of his namesake. Iron Man also had the hero Dark Angel grant the armor anti-magic protections, making it impervious to Malekith’s usual tricks. Add giant claws, a grappling hook, and cluster bombs of iron nails, and Iron Man could carve his way through the Dark Elves. When these villains finally confronted Iron Man, he was prepared to deploy the Cold Iron Armor. It was an absolute massacre. By the end, the Armored Avenger had practically become a bogeyman to the Dark Elves.

Iron Man and Black Panther are the two most iconic armored heroes in Marvel Comics. An evil future version of Iron Man designed the Armored Avengers’ Model 21 Stealth Armor specifically to counter the King of Wakanda. The suit made practically all of Black Panther’s gadgets and skills worthless. Fitting for a stealth armor, the suit let Iron Man become invisible and imperceptible to Black Panther’s enhanced senses and scanning instruments. The suit is also made of a special material that can neutralize the vibranium in Black Panther’s suit, rendering it useless. For offensive capabilities, the Stealth Suit can generate deadly plasma that can even hurt Thor. Even more, the Stealth Suit has an AI that can instantly study and counter an opponent’s fighting styles. Although the heroic, present-day Iron Man never donned the Stealth Armor, his tendency to build suits designed to defeat his fellow heroes means he’ll inevitably make it to fight Black Panther.

Iron Man normally operates on Earth, but when he officially joined the Guardians of the Galaxy, he knew he needed an all-new suit. Capable of interplanetary travel thanks to powerful cosmic thrusters, the Model 44 Deep Space Armor is among the fastest armors Iron Man has ever built. The suit is also strong enough to withstand blows from Black Bolt and is outfitted with Iron Man’s AI assistant P.E.P.P.E.R. The Deep Space Armor is highly adaptable, with access to numerous extensions, including the Saturn V armor, which makes it bigger and tougher for terrestrial battles. Tony doesn’t even have to worry about Earth being unprotected, as he can remotely control his other suits from light-years away. Altogether, this suit has the power and versatility to be one of Iron Man’s primary armors. Space is the final frontier, and Iron Man’s drive to push innovation led him to reach for the stars.

articles.content:
The ice appears to be thawing between Netflix and Cannes .

The streamer, which hasn't debuted a film at the festival in almost a decade due to France's strict rules around theatrical releases, is eyeing a return to the south of France in 2027, Variety has learned. Ted Sarandos suggested as much earlier this year, when he told Variety he hoped to “do something special" for Cannes' 80th edition. Now it turns out that Cannes boss Thierry Frémaux has also been making a push to bring Joel Coen's "Jack of Spades" to the festival for more than a year, sources say. Netflix declined to comment. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The American gothic mystery, starring Josh O'Connor, Patsy Ferran, Frances McDormand, Lesley Manville and Damian Lewis, was at one point expected to be ready for this year's Cannes, then Venice, but is now on track for next May. Coen also has a strong relationship with Frémaux, who honored him alongside his brother Ethan at Lyon's Lumière Film Festival.

But there's a catch. Netflix recently acquired "Jack of Spades," complicating plans for what would otherwise have been a natural Cannes contender.

Under the festival's rules, all films competing for the Palme d'Or must receive a theatrical release in France. That would trigger the country's strict windowing regulations, forcing Netflix to wait 15 months before making the film available to French subscribers — something the streamer isn't prepared to do. And while Cannes would very much like to have Netflix back, it isn't willing to bend its rules to make that happen.

That means the only way for Netflix to return to Cannes with "Jack of Spades" would be out of competition, which has been a deal-breaker for Sarandos. Sources say Frémaux has been trying to convince Netflix and Sarandos that an out-of-competition premiere can be just as prestigious as a competition slot, pointing to the recent examples of Martin Scorsese's Apple-backed "Killers of the Flower Moon" and Tom Cruise's "Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning," both of which made a major splash on the Croisette without competing for the Palme d'Or. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But recent changes could help smooth the path towards a Netflix comeback on the Croisette. The streamer's newly-appointed chief content officer Peter Rice is a longtime friend of Cannes who has known Frémaux since his days at Searchlight. His arrival could help bring the two sides closer after years of tensions over theatrical releases.

Netflix may also have good reason to seek a return to Cannes. After losing a few big-name filmmakers, the streamer could be looking to ramp up its prestige profile. While it has increasingly turned to Venice to launch major awards contenders, including Guillermo del Toro's "Frankenstein" and Noah Baumbach's "Jay Kelly," Cannes remains the world's biggest film festival and arguably the most powerful platform for launching auteur-driven movies.

Netflix knows that better than most. Despite not bringing its own movies to the festival in 10 years, it has snapped up several on the ground there. In 2024, it bought Jacques Audiard's "Emilia Pérez" which went on earn 13 Oscar nominations and win two Oscars, including best actress for Zoe Saldana. This year, it acquired "La Bola Negra," now its main hope for awards season — with many tipping it for best picture.

"Jack of Spades" would seem a perfect fit for the festival, where Joel Coen is one of its favorite auteurs. Alongside his brother Ethan, the director has brought films including "Barton Fink," which won the Palme d'Or and best director awards, "No Country for Old Men" and "Inside Llewyn Davis."

Netflix hasn't taken a film to Cannes since 2017, when it premiered both Bong Joon-ho's "Okja" and Noah Baumbach's "The Meyerowitz Stories." It sparked an outcry from French exhibitors, prompting the festival to change its rules the following year to require competition films to receive theatrical releases in France.

The streamer has, however, softened its stance on theatrical releases considerably. "La Bola Negra" is in the middle of a 46-day theatrical rollout, the longest Netflix has given any of its films to date. Next year, "Narnia: The Magician's Nephew" will have an exclusive theatrical run, as will Taika Waititi's animated take on Roald Dahl, "Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory."

articles.summary: He served as head film buyer and oversaw Canadian operations and real estate ventures during his nearly three decades with the company.
articles.content:
Thom Velde, who served as head film buyer at AMC Theatres during his 27 years with the chain, died of cancer on Oct. 31 in Rancho Mirage, his family announced. He was 83.

Velde negotiated film agreements with domestic and international studios and oversaw AMC's Canadian operations and real estate ventures during his long tenure at the company.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos Says He Was "Heavily Involved" in Casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond
articles.summary: The Amazon founder told a conference Tuesday that he and the film leadership were initially biased against Pattinson before realizing they found their man.
articles.content:
The names Bezos, Jeff Bezos . And he just chose the next James Bond .

The Amazon founder and chairman told a conference Tuesday that he “was heavily involved” in selecting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond, working alongside the Amazon MGM leadership team, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, and director Denis Villeneuve.

“We ran a really tight process, and we made the final decision on Friday,” Bezos said at Semafor's Silicon Valley & The World conference. “There were a big group initially, and we selected down to five finalists, and then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists.”

By now, those finalists are well known: Callum Turner, Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult, and Pattinson, the man who ultimately secured Bond's tuxedo.

Bezos says that they ran an elaborate screen test, with each actor performing three scenes with full costumes and sets.

“They were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob and his performances, and it was kind of immediately un-debated. Denis, the director was, we all sort of gravitated to him,” Bezos recalled. “By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he's already so famous. We sort of thought, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious: He is James Bond.”

The casting of Pattinson is without question the biggest move yet by Amazon since it acquired MGM and since it bought out the Broccoli family for control of the franchise.

The irony is not lost on people that the Bond franchise is filled with tech tycoons and media industrialists as villains, from Hugo Drax in Moonraker to Max Zorin in A View to a Kill to Elliott Carver in Tomorrow Never Dies .

Now James Bond is firmly controlled by one of the world's richest man, and a mogul whose empire spans tech, media, entertainment and even rockets into space. And this time he was the one helping to call the shots.

articles.title: 5 Sentinels That Could Destroy the MCU's X-Men Before They Get Started
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics The X-Men are coming to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU), and there is no telling what villains will arrive after the originally announced Mister Sinister. However, before Mister Sinister ever shows up in the MCU, the Sentinels are coming. The trailers for Avengers: Doomsday clearly show Doctor Doom raising an army of Sentinels out of […]
articles.content:
The Sentinels from the comics are not just giant robots programmed to hunt down mutants. There are also several Sentinels that have morphed over the years into even deadlier villains, and some of these can even adapt and hide in plain sight, making them more of a threat than just giant robots that shoot rays at mutants. These Sentinels could show up in the MCU and present an immediate threat to the mutant race.

Karima Shapandar first appeared in X-Men Unlimited #27 (2000) by Chris Claremont, Brett Booth, and Ron Lim. She was an Indian police officer whom Bastion's forces converted into a Prime Sentinel, one of the human-turned-cyborg sleeper agents that became mutant-killing machines once they detected a mutant was nearby. As a Prime Sentinel, she has superhuman strength and speed, flight, adaptive regeneration, energy blasts, microwave emitters, and limited machine control.

Her debut story is also Neal Shaara's origin as the new Thunderbird. Karima saves him from an attack in Calcutta. The two fall in love, and after her conversion, she warns him she will soon be forced to destroy him. She joined the X-Men, but her programming was accidentally reactivated later, making her a villain again. She was also much stronger by then because Beast had rebuilt her and enhanced her powers. A trusted ally who becomes a mutant-hunting sleeper Sentinel would be a great twist in the MCU.

Bastion made his full first appearance in Uncanny X-Men #333 (1996) by Scott Lobdell and Pasqual Ferry. He is a being who was the merged combination of Master Mold and Nimrod, reborn without memories after the X-Men blasted them through the Siege Perilous. He has immunity to telepathic probes and mutant powers. He also has the powers of adaptation, technoforming, teleportation, and technopathy. Finally, he has full control over regular Sentinels and can turn humans into Prime Sentinels.

He has immense defensive powers, as not even Jean Grey could do anything to him with her Omega-level telepathic abilities. He was responsible for the crossover storyline “Operation: Zero Tolerance,” which was the 1997 event that crossed over every mutant title that summer. In “Angels and Demons,” he was back and infected Steven Lang, Cameron Hodge, Bolivar Trask, William Stryker, and Graydon Creed with the Transmode Virus. As a human-looking Sentinel, he could be a perfect villain in the MCU if the government determines the mutants to be a threat.

The Wild Sentinels debuted in New X-Men #114 (2001) by Grant Morrison and Frank Quitely, and they were responsible for the worst thing to ever happen to mutants in Marvel Comics. They were built by a forgotten Master Mold unit hidden in the highlands of Ecuador. Their form is unique and explains their name, as they cannibalize scrap metal and raw materials into highly variable but functional body types. They can also create more of themselves in an effort to make Sentinels self-sustaining.

Cassandra Nova used Donald Trask to gain control of them, and she sent them to destroy Genosha and kill 16 million mutants in New X-Men #115 (2001). This was also shown as an event in the X-Men '97 series, and in the comics, it still stands as one of the most destructive moments in X-Men history. A Sentinel that can create more of itself and is powerful enough to slaughter an entire nation would be one of the most frightening things that the MCU could ever introduce.

Master Mold first appeared in The X-Men #15 (1965) by Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, and Jay Gavin. Bolivar Trask built Master Mold as a supercomputer to control Sentinel construction. The problem was that it captured Trask and tried to take over humanity, and Trask had to sacrifice himself to destroy it. This is a giant Sentinel that builds other Sentinels, and it doesn't just target mutants. It actually threatened to destroy half of the United States if its demands weren't met.

As mentioned earlier, Bastion was created from the merging of Master Mold and Nimrod, and Master Mold is where Bastion gained the ability to build and control Sentinels. While Bastion is scary since he can look almost human, Master Mold would be a scarier addition to the MCU because it is a giant Sentinel that is more intelligent and deadly than the rest. In the MCU, Master Mold could be the factory that pumps out the Sentinels that hunt the mutants.

Nimrod is a different Sentinel because he comes from the future. Nimrod first appeared in Uncanny X-Men #191 (1984) by Chris Claremont and John Romita Jr. He comes from the “Days of Future Past” timeline, and he followed Rachel Summers back in time to the present-day Marvel-616 world. He arrived in a Manhattan subway, blasted a mugger, and saw anti-mutant graffiti, realizing that mutants exist here too.

Thanks to the tech from the future, he is more durable than other Sentinels, as his body is self-healing and self-replicating, and he also has an internal translocator that displaces matter. He merged with Master Mold to create Bastion, but this also led Bastion to create an endless horde of Nimrods. Nimrod was also one of the key weapons that helped ruin the mutants' utopian home on Krakoa. The MCU could bring in Nimrod as a Sentinel from the future to threaten the new young mutants emerging on this Earth.

What Sentinels do you think we will see arrive in the MCU to threaten the mutants? Let us know your favorite Sentinels in the comments below.

Andrew Stearn has been appointed as President of Foolscap, with Alie Rivier Gutman as Vice President of TV Development and Lulu Dillon as Vice President of Feature & TV Production. The company has a first-look deal at 20th TV, with projects set up at 20th, A24, Hulu, FX, Onyx, Paramount +, ABC, Mattel and Fifth Season. articles.title: ‘Dancing With the Stars’: All 34 Winners
articles.summary: A Tony winner, several Olympians, Super Bowl champions, Bachelorettes and the Irwin siblings are just a few of the stars who have won the coveted mirrorball trophy throughout the show’s 20-year history.
articles.content:
Kelly Monaco won the inaugural season of DWTS in 2005 alongside pro dancer Alec Mazo. That was far from the last time the General Hospital actress would be seen in the ballroom, as she notably competed on the 15th season with Valentin Chmerkovskiy as her partner.

Her double spin as a contestant on the series makes her one of six winners to return to the show to compete for a second time. She also appeared on season 25 to perform a trio number with Terrell Owens and Cheryl Burke, alongside six other former competitors.

Drew Lachey, former member of 98 Degrees and brother to Love Is Blind host Nick Lachey, picked up his mirrorball during season two. Partnered with Cheryl Burke , he returned for season 15 where he competed with Anna Trebunskaya.

Despite being named the show’s champion on his first DWTS turn, he was eliminated during week three during his second shot. However, Lachey, alongside Monaco, is still penned in the DWTS history books as one of the few winners to compete on the show more than once.

Cheryl Burke extended her winning streak into season three with Emmitt Smith. The former Dallas Cowboys running back made history with his 2006 win as the first (of four) NFL players to win DWTS . Plus, Smith is a part of the hexad of past champions who returned for season 15, where he was partnered with Cheryl once more.

Olympian Apolo Anton Ohno won the fourth DWTS installment, notably earning current co-host Julianne Hough her first mirrorball. Plus, Julianne's season four victory also set the record for the youngest pro dancer to reign supreme, as she won the competition series at just 18 years old. (And she quickly made another record one year later.) Ohno also returned for season 15, and placed fifth.

Julianne Hough followed in Cheryl Burke’s footsteps in 2007 by winning the show for the second year in a row with racing driver Hélio Castroneves. The Indy 500 racer came back to DWTS in 2015 for season 15, where he placed 10th.

Olympic champion figure skater Kristi Yamaguchi translated her gold-medal winning talents into the DWTS ballroom in 2008, where she won season six. Her triumph saw Mark Ballas earn his first win as a pro dancer, one of many more to come.

Brooke Burke and current judge Derek Hough won the show’s seventh installment, which led to years of them both being intertwined with the DWTS family. Coming onto the show as a model and TV host, Burke offered the latter talent to the series as a DWTS co-host from season 10-17.

Brooke's win was also served as Derek's first win. While this list is intended to highlight the winners of the show, it’s also important to note that each celebrity victory also parlayed into the careers of the pro dancers that make up the series.

Shawn Johnson became the first gymnast to win DWTS in 2009. Partnered with Mark Ballas (marking his second victory), the gold medalist reappeared on the series for (you guessed it!) season 15 alongside Derek Hough.

Donny & Marie star Donny Osmond took his turn on the competition ballroom dance series in 2009, where he won season nine alongside Kym Johnson. He is notably the oldest person to ever win the show, as he was 51 at the time he was crowned champion.

Before Nicole Scherzinger won her Tony Award , she reigned victorious on DWTS . The former Pussycat Dolls singer was partnered with Derek Hough for the landmark 10th season.

Derek Hough won his fourth DWTS installment during season 11, with Dirty Dancing actress Jennifer Grey. Her first dance paid tribute to the film, a Viennese waltz set to “These Arms of Mine” by Otis Redding from the movie.

Grey long held the record for the most perfect scores in a season, setting it initially with six. She stands as the eldest woman to win DWTS , and she was 50 when she secured the title.

Former Pittsburgh Steelers player Hines Ward nabbed the DWTS season 12 champion title in 2012 with Kym Johnson.

Actor and Army veteran J.R. Martinez won season 13 alongside pro Karina Smirnoff, marking her first DWTS win. Following his victory, Martinez told The Hollywood Reporter he was “so grateful that I was able to be part of the journey to help get her first mirrorball trophy.”

Donald Driver, a former Green Bay Packers player, and Peta Murgatroyd won season 14 of DWTS . Following the triumph, he reflected on becoming another NFL star to win the mirrorball with THR .

“It took me 13 years to win the Super Bowl,” Driver joked. “I’m just glad it took me one season to win the mirrorball.”

The coveted 15th season of the show, better known as DWTS: All-Stars , was ultimately won by Melissa Rycroft . She was a contestant on The Bachelor season 13, and got engaged to Jason Mesnick, though he called off the engagement shortly after.

After her run as a Bachelor Nation star, she quickly pivoted to appearing on DWTS for season eight. (It’s a trend that would later catch wind for contestants in the franchise to go on the competitive dance show directly after their time searching for love on TV.) There, she placed third, before returning for season 15 and winning the mirrorball alongside Tony Dovolani.

American Idol alum Kellie Pickler returned to the competitive reality TV circuit in 2013, earning first place on season 16 of DWTS . She was partnered with Derek Hough, and notably beat out Zendaya for the top spot in the competition.

Marking the second time Derek Hough won consecutive seasons, Amber Riley was the show’s 17th winner. The Glee star and Derek had quite the impressive turn, tying the then-record for the highest first week score, receiving three nines from the judges. In total, she had five perfect scores throughout the season, which led her to nab the season 17 champion title.

Riley is also notably the first African American woman to win a regular, mainstay season of DWTS . (Melissa Rycroft won All-Stars .)

Olympic silver medalist Meryl Davis nabbed the DWTS mirrorball in 2014 alongside Makism Chmerkovskiy. She notably competed against her ice skating partner Charlie White, who placed fifth. At the time, she broke the record for the most perfect scored dances, with six.

Long before he became a co-host of DWTS , Alfonso Ribeiro won the show in 2014. Earning Witney Carson her first mirrorball as well, the duo were a force during the 19th installment. He matched Amber Riley’s record for best first week score ever, after earning 36/40 (meaning he received four nines from each judge).

Rumer Willis won the landmark 20th season of the competitive ballroom show alongside Valentin Chmerkovskiy, in his first win ever . Daughter to Demi Moore and Bruce Willis, Rumer matched Meryl Davis’ score of most perfect dances by a competitor.

One of the most heartwrenching journeys on DWTS came with Bindi Irwin’s season 21 appearance with her partner Derek Hough. Son of the beloved Steve Irwin, Bindi was the first winner to completely blow out the once-set record of most perfect dances. Jennifer Grey and Rumer Willis each had six, though Bindi earned eight perfect scores.

During Most Memorable Year week, she paid tribute to her late father with a touching contemporary that is ingrained in DWTS history. Competing on the show in 2015, her younger brother Robert Irwin later joined the show, partaking in season 34 of the series in 2025, exactly 10 years post-her tenure in the competition. After his win, they became the first sibling duo to both win DWTS .

Nyle DiMarco had a historic run during season 22 of DWTS , becoming the first deaf person to win the series. Hailing from one of the final cycles of America’s Next Top Model , DiMarco and Peta Murgatroyd’s time on the competitive reality show broke down barriers.

Another gymnast to be crowned a mirrorball champion, Laurie Hernandez won season 23 with Valentin Chmerkovskiy. She is the youngest DWTS winner ever , as she won the show when she was a mere 16-years-old in 2016.

Rashad Jennings is the fourth NFL player to win DWTS . He won with Emma Slater, marking her first and only win as a pro dancer in 2017.

Jordan Fisher and Lindsay Arnold won the show during 2017’s fall season. Fisher’s time on DWTS was record-breaking, as he notably earned nine perfect scores throughout season 25, taking over Bindi Irwin’s achievement of eight.

Olympic bronze medalist Adam Rippon won the first and only season of DWTS: Athletes . Sporting a cast of (you guessed it) only athletes, season 26 was a condensed, four-week installment that saw Jenna Johnson win her first mirrorball.

Bobby Bones’ DWTS win is one of the most controversial conquests in the show's 20 year run. Dancing with his partner Sharna Burgess, the radio host had the lowest judges scores of the finalists during season 27. His win caused a shift in the DWTS universe — one that signified that viewers' votes could successfully influence a celebrity to win a show without having the scoring to back it up.

Hannah Brown became the second Bachelorette to appear on DWTS during season 28, and the first to win, with her partner Alan Bersten, marking his first and only win.

Following directly behind her fellow franchise leader, Kaitlyn Bristowe won DWTS during the show’s first season set in the middle of the COVID-19 pandemic. In the fall of 2020, Bristowe earned the title of being the second Bachelorette to earn the mirrorball with her partner Artem Chigvintsev.

Iman Shumpert reigned supreme during another milestone season of DWTS . On season 30, he earned the title of the first NBA star to win the show, also earning Daniella Karagach ’s first mirrorball.

Longtime DWTS champion pro Mark Ballas made his grand return to the ballroom after six installments off for an impressive season-long run with Charli D’Amelio. The first TikTok star to join the franchise’s cast, Charli earned six perfect scores during her run on the show. She is also a part of the first duo of non-spousal family members to compete on DWTS , as her mother, Heidi D’Amelio, also appeared on season 31.

Xochitl Gomez won the mirrorball trophy in the fall of 2023. She was partnered with Valentin Chmerkovskiy, notably standing as one of the youngest winners of the show, as she was 17 when she snatched the title.

Joey Graziadei is the most recent winner of DWTS , and the only Bachelor to ever win the competitive ballroom series. He was partnered with Jenna Johnson, totaling her number of wins up to two.

Robert Irwin and Witney Carson won the coveted mirrorball of DWTS ‘ 2025 installment, putting a cap on one of the show's most popular seasons ever. Following in the footsteps of his sister, Robert's win extended the Irwin family's impact on the competitive ballroom dance series. Plus, they are the only pair of siblings to both win DWTS .

The winner of Dancing With the Stars season 35 is soon-to-be-announced when the finale airs on Nov. 24. With the semi-final round of competition about to kick off, the champion will be one of the following celebrities still in the running: Tatyana Ali , Ezra Frech , Amber Glenn , Maura Higgins, Harry Shum Jr. or Connor Wood .

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence's 'Hunger Games' Premiere Look Proves the Boudoir Coat Is Back: Here's Where to Shop Similar Styles Online
articles.summary: Naked dressing out. Fur, in. At the premiere of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" on Monday night, Jennifer Lawrence embraced one of the biggest outerwear trends this season: the fur-trimmed satin coat. The actress, who reprises her beloved role as Katniss in the prequel film, walked the carpet in a floor-length black silk […]
articles.content:
At the premiere of " The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping " on Monday night, Jennifer Lawrence embraced one of the biggest outerwear trends this season: the fur-trimmed satin coat.

The actress, who reprises her beloved role as Katniss in the prequel film, walked the carpet in a floor-length black silk coat from Jonathan Anderson's Dior Pre-Fall 2026 collection . The robe-like design featured an oversized white fur collar, colorful floral embroidery cascading down one side and a dramatic front slit, which Lawrence paired with black satin mules by Gianvito Rossi and vintage diamond-and-onyx earrings from Fred Leighton. Related Stories ‘SNL’: Druski Dons Whiteface as Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’ Parody ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker Pitched Nathan Fielder a Collaboration After Watching ‘You Can See Everything’: ‘I Put It Out in the Water’

The boudoir-inspired silhouette, which combines silky fabrics, sweeping hemlines and oversized fur collars, has become a favorite among designers and celebrities alike. London-based designer Conner Ives helped popularize the look with his demi-couture silk robes, first introduced on his Fall 2025 runway and subsequently worn by Zoë Kravitz, Sienna Miller, Hailey Bieber and Kendall Jenner. Lawrence herself wore one of Ives' black fur-trimmed designs at the "Die, My Love" premiere in London last year.

The trend extends well beyond Ives. Miu Miu incorporated fuzzy fur trimming into distressed leather outerwear for Fall 2026, while Dries Van Noten embraced satin finishes on its runway. Balenciaga, Zuhair Murad and Stéphane Rolland have also explored dramatic, robe-inspired silhouettes in their recent couture collections.

While Lawrence's Dior creation and Ives' silk robes carry luxury price tags, shoppers don't have to spend thousands to get a similar look. More affordable retailers, including Zara, Mango and ASOS, have embraced exaggerated faux-fur collars, belted silhouettes and floor-sweeping coats.
